column1: *** THIMM — STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE, AND HERE IS THE MEASUREMENT ***
column2: all 2,500 FamilySearch collections were enumerated and filtered for Prussia.

column1: what FamilySearch has indexed for the Prussian provinces
column2: POSEN, Catholic and Lutheran Church Records 1430-1998 — 11,671,064 records · SILESIA 1551-1992 — 4,516,465 · POMERANIA 1544-1966 — 2,163,005 · BRANDENBURG AND POSEN Church Book Duplicates 1700-1875 — 1,700,252 · WEST PRUSSIA, Catholic and Lutheran Church Records · and a general Prussia set 1580-1974 — 193,105.

column1: AND FOR EAST PRUSSIA
column2: *** TWO COLLECTIONS. BOTH KÖNIGSBERG FUNERAL SERMONS. BOTH IMAGE-ONLY, WITH ZERO INDEXED RECORDS, COVERING 1597-1794 AND 1700-1900. *** There is no East Prussian church-record index at FamilySearch at all.

column1: so the Thimms cannot be searched by name
column2: Johanna Thimm was born at SAUERBAUM, KREIS RÖSSEL on 25 March 1871, and her parents ANTON THIMM (b. 16 July 1840) and ELISABETH THIMM (b. 15 March 1845) are already in this archive. NO NAME INDEX ANYWHERE REACHES THEIR PARISH. This also explains, retrospectively, why a search for LUWINSKI across all of FamilySearch returned 71 records and not one East Prussian: it is the index that stops at the provincial border, not the family.

column1: the only two routes, and both were established yesterday
column2: (1) the GROSS BÖSSAU parish register, which the catalogue says covers Sauerbaum — nine films, EIGHT OF THEM NOT DIGITISED, and the two that matter (Taufen 1793-1890 and the civil birth copies 1881-1958) both answer "film number not found". (2) The originals: the Archiwum Archidiecezji Warmińskiej and the state archive, both at Olsztyn.

column1: AND ONE THING THE ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD AND HAD NOT JOINED UP
column2: *** JOHANNA THIMM DIED AT ZEUTERN, near Bruchsal, on 30 October 1955. AUGUSTE "LIZZY" LUWINSKI DIED AT KRAICHTAL ON 22 JUNE 1975. ZEUTERN IS A DISTRICT OF KRAICHTAL. *** The East Prussia page lists them as two different places and they are one place. Mother and daughter died in the same small town in Baden-Württemberg, twenty years apart, having left East Prussia, passed through Berlin and ended in the west.

column1: and it bears on a candidate raised this morning
column2: Johanna's recorded addresses include RICHARD-WAGNER-STRASSE 42, CHARLOTTENBURG, from 24 July 1932. The 1957 Berlin directory candidate for Lizzy is "Fricke Auguste, Rentnerin, CHARLOTTENBURG 1, KAISER-FRIEDRICH-STRASSE 79". THE SAME DISTRICT, a few streets apart. That does not confirm the candidate — but the family demonstrably had a Charlottenburg address, which this archive did not weigh this morning, and Lizzy's own death at Kraichtal in 1975 shows she ended up where her mother had.

column1: *** SCHMUL — NOT IN THE CHURCH BOOKS, AND THERE IS A REASON ***
column2: the Posen collection holds THIRTY-THREE people with the exact surname SCHMUL. ALL THIRTY-THREE WERE READ. There is no FRIEDERIKE, and there is no Schubin marriage of 1874.

column1: what is there, and it is Jewish
column2: WOLF SCHMUL and BEILA LEPOTKE, with a daughter RICKE SCHMUL born 15 January 1832 · ISIDOR SCHMUL and LIEBCHEN KATZ, daughter Hedvigis born 2 September 1903 · HEDVIGIS SCHMUL born 1881, married Leon Victor Zemmel at Schwersenz on 17 November 1903 · Theophilus Schmul and Maria Krüger. There is also a Protestant Schmul line at Labischin in Kreis Schubin from 1787.

column1: A NEAR MISS WORTH NAMING SO NOBODY ELSE CHASES IT
column2: *** RICKE IS A DIMINUTIVE OF FRIEDERIKE, and Ricke Schmul is the daughter of a Jewish couple in Posen. *** But she was born in JANUARY 1832, which would make her forty-two at the 1874 marriage and FIFTY-TWO WHEN JACOB WAS BORN IN 1884. She is the right name in the right province and the wrong generation. NOT A CANDIDATE.

column1: WHY FRIEDERIKE IS NOT IN THAT COLLECTION
column2: IT IS A COLLECTION OF CHURCH BOOKS. A Jewish marriage is not in one. Before 1874 a Jewish marriage in Prussia was recorded in the Jewish community's own register; PRUSSIAN CIVIL REGISTRATION BEGAN ON 1 OCTOBER 1874, so a Szubin marriage in 1874 falls either side of that line and is a Judenregister entry or a STANDESAMT entry. Neither is in a church-book index.

column1: *** AND THE ARCHIVE ALREADY HAS A LIVE REQUEST TO EXACTLY THE RIGHT PLACE ***
column2: ARCHIWUM PAŃSTWOWE W BYDGOSZCZY holds Standesamt Schubin, and this archive wrote to them on 15 September for STANDESAMT SCHUBIN 1884 — Jacob Leibholz's birth. They acknowledged, with a warning that a complicated query can take over a month. THE 1874 MARRIAGE IS THE SAME REGISTRY OFFICE AND THE SAME ARCHIVE. It can be added to the thread that is already open.

column1: and it is worth more than the birth certificate
column2: A PRUSSIAN MARRIAGE CERTIFICATE OF 1874 NAMES BOTH SETS OF PARENTS, with ages and occupations. It would give FRIEDERIKE SCHMUL'S FATHER AND MOTHER and SALLY LEIBHOLZ'S — the generation ABOVE the great-grandparents on the chart, which this archive has never reached on either side.

column1: A NEGATIVE NOT PUBLISHED, BECAUSE THE CONTROL KILLED IT
column2: Geneteka, the Polish Genealogical Society's index, was searched for LEIBHOLZ marriages in Kujawsko-Pomorskie 1860-1890 and returned nothing. THE CONTROL RETURNED NOTHING TOO: the same query for KOWALSKI — the commonest Polish surname there is — also gave "Pozycji 0 z 0". The URL parameters are wrong, or the search needs a posted form. SO THE LEIBHOLZ ZERO MEANS NOTHING AND IS NOT RECORDED AS A NEGATIVE. Geneteka remains untested.

column1: # ——— GENETEKA, DONE PROPERLY 20 SEPTEMBER 2026, AND THE EARLIER FAILURE IS EXPLAINED ———
*** THE CAUSE OF THE FAILED CONTROL, AND IT IS A ONE-CHARACTER BUG ***
column2: the earlier attempt searched with the province parameter w=04kp, on the reasonable assumption that kp stands for kujawsko-pomorskie. *** IT IS NOT A VALID CODE. *** Geneteka's province codes are positional: 01ds dolnośląskie, 02kp KUJAWSKO-POMORSKIE, 03lb lubelskie, 04ls LUBUSKIE, 05ld łódzkie, and so on. A code that does not exist makes the select fall back silently to 01ds, dolnośląskie — so every query ran against the wrong province and returned nothing, INCLUDING THE KOWALSKI CONTROL. The control did its job: it said the query was broken, and it was.

column1: and the same trap in a second form
column2: the results table is filled by AJAX after the page loads. A plain fetch of the search URL returns the page shell with an EMPTY TABLE, which reads exactly like a zero. The rows only exist in a rendered browser. Two ways to get a false negative out of one site.

column1: *** NOW THE ANSWER, WITH THE CONTROL PASSING ***
column2: w=02kp, surname KOWALSKI, births: thousands of rows from 1621 onwards. THE QUERY WORKS. On the same query shape: LEIBHOLZ in kujawsko-pomorskie returns ZERO for births and ZERO for marriages, and LEIBHOLZ in wielkopolskie returns ZERO for births and ZERO for marriages.

column1: SCHMUL, which does return something
column2: wielkopolskie marriages, surname SCHMUL: EIGHTEEN records, and they are fuzzy matches across Szmul, Szmił, Schmul, Szmiel and Szmielewski. Parishes: Lwówek 1745 · Przedecz 1789 · Pyzdry 1821, 1822, 1824, 1825 · Turek 1837 · Młodojewo 1880 · Brdów 1882 · DĄBIE (MOJŻ.) 1887, 1893, 1905 · Krotoszyn USC 1894 · Kraszewice 1900 · Grodzisk Wielkopolski USC 1901 · Gniezno 1907 · Pniewy USC 1914 · Koło 1919. *** NOT ONE OF THEM IS AT SZUBIN. ***

column1: *** AND THE REASON NO SZUBIN JEWISH RECORD CAN EVER APPEAR ***
column2: SZUBIN IS IN GENETEKA. It is parish id 13066 in kujawsko-pomorskie, and its indexed registers begin in 1715. *** IT IS THE CATHOLIC PARISH. *** Geneteka marks Jewish registers "(mojż.)" and Protestant ones "(ewang.)" — and KUJAWSKO-POMORSKIE CONTAINS NO (mojż.) PARISH AT ALL, not one, across all 358 entries in its list. The Jewish community registers of Szubin are not in this index and nothing about the surname searches can change that.

column1: so the row's conclusion, stated at last with a control behind it
column2: GENETEKA CANNOT ANSWER THE SZUBIN QUESTION. Sally Leibholz's marriage to Friederike Schmul on 24 November 1874 is a Jewish or civil record of a town whose Jewish registers this index does not hold. THE LETTER TO BYDGOSZCZ IS THE ONLY ROUTE, and it is drafted as requests/30-SEND-THIS-to-bydgoszcz.txt and unsent. That is now a tested statement rather than an assumption.
